chunks: Mis'am ibn Abd al-Malik narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"If a servant performs ten pilgrimages, the Hajj of Islam is incumbent upon him if he has the ability to do so."

key_terms.اسْتَطَاعَ: To have the ability/capacity (financial and physical)
key_terms.حَجَّةُ الْإِسْلَامِ: The obligatory Hajj, the first one that becomes due

ai.seo_question: Does performing multiple Hajjs replace the one obligatory Hajj?
ai.summary: Reported by Mism' ibn Abd al-Malik from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith establishes that the single obligatory Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam) is distinct from additional voluntary pilgrimages, meaning extra acts do not substitute for the primary duty. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that the condition of *istita'ah* (ability) remains the sole determinant for the obligation, regardless of one's history of performing other Hajjs.
